title: Restore access for a service account
goal: Repair ownership/group access without broadening permissions or running the service as root.
challenge: Identify the locked non-login account for ll-access.service and why it cannot read /etc/learning-lab/access.conf. Restore only root-owner/service-group read access at 0640, prove an unrelated account still cannot read it, and verify the service.

steps.command: getent passwd ll-service; id ll-service; sudo passwd -S ll-service; ls -ld /etc/learning-lab; ls -l /etc/learning-lab/access.conf
steps.explanation: Inspect account shell, lock state, ancestors and file ownership. A non-login account can still run a system service.
steps.expected: Locked ll-service with nologin shell; config is root:root 0640.

steps.command: sudo runuser -u ll-service -- cat /etc/learning-lab/access.conf; sudo systemctl start ll-access.service; sudo journalctl -u ll-access.service -n 8 --no-pager
steps.explanation: Run a read as the real service user, then correlate the unit failure. sudo is used only to adopt that guest identity.

steps.command: sudo cp -p /etc/learning-lab/access.conf /etc/learning-lab/access.conf.before; sudo chgrp ll-service /etc/learning-lab/access.conf; sudo chmod 0640 /etc/learning-lab/access.conf
steps.explanation: Keep root ownership; grant only the service group read. Do not use 777 or change the unit User to root.

steps.command: sudo runuser -u ll-service -- cat /etc/learning-lab/access.conf; sudo runuser -u nobody -- cat /etc/learning-lab/access.conf
steps.explanation: Verify both permitted and denied access. nobody is only an existing guest test identity.
steps.expected: Service user reads; unrelated nobody gets permission denied.

steps.command: sudo systemctl restart ll-access.service; sleep 1; sudo journalctl -u ll-access.service -n 8 --no-pager
steps.explanation: Allow a brief startup interval, then verify a new LAB_READY from the repaired invocation. If absent, inspect status and reread the journal; do not infer readiness just from restart returning.

steps.command: sudo systemctl stop ll-access.service; systemctl is-active ll-access.service
steps.explanation: After recording readiness, stop only this unit. Keep the repaired configuration and evidence.
steps.expected: inactive; a nonzero is-active status is expected.

hints: A service needs directory search and file read; inspect ancestors as well as the file.
The owner can stay root while the service group receives read permission.
Reading successfully as root does not prove service-account access.
review: I verified permitted and denied reads under actual guest identities.
The worker remained unprivileged and no world access was granted.
coverage: Partial LPIC-1 104.5 ownership/group access; 107.1 limited-account inspection; LPIC-2 202.1 service context. Guest-only administration; completion records self-review, not verified assessment. No score.
